verdict.summary: Strategy is no longer usefully valued as an enterprise-software vendor: the common stock is a leveraged residual claim behind 843,775 BTC, $6.67 billion of debt and $15.46 billion of preferred liquidation preference at June 30. Q2 software revenue improved 6.9% to $122.4 million, led by subscription services, but that cash engine is immaterial beside an $8.33 billion GAAP operating loss caused by bitcoin fair-value accounting. The investable question is whether repeated common and preferred issuance can add BTC per diluted share faster than dividends, interest and mNAV compression consume value. Management raised $17.06 billion through ATMs year to date and held a $3.75 billion USD reserve, providing more than 2.1 years of stated preferred-dividend and interest coverage. That reduces forced-sale risk, not structural leverage. The C grade is defensible for financing access and software recurrence, but the equity remains a complex, reflexive bitcoin vehicle. With the setup still inactive, conviction requires both the stated technical activation and evidence that incremental capital remains accretive per share.

The platform still holds $246 billion of customer assets, roughly 11.2% of total crypto market capitalization, and average USDC balances on Coinbase products reached $20 billion. Yet GAAP net loss was $359.5 million, stock compensation was $238.3 million and rebuilt current EV is about 25.0x the issuer's roughly $1.878 billion trailing adjusted EBITDA on both Class A and Class B shares. Q2 adjusted EBITDA remained positive at $207.8 million, but Q3 subscription-and-services guidance of $500-$580 million does not remove sensitivity to rates, stablecoin economics or spot volumes. Buybacks have offset more than 85% of stock-compensation issuance since Q4 2024, which is useful but not free. Publication stance: structurally advantaged exchange and custody infrastructure, financially cyclical equity, and no chase before the existing activation confirms.

Long Ridge and Matagorda create credible power-site optionality for AI/HPC, but neither is a contracted AI revenue stream in the quarter. A D+ quality grade is therefore appropriate: scale and assets are real, earnings quality and leverage are weak. The current trade remains watch-only until $11.60 confirms; bitcoin rallies cannot substitute for improving cost per hash and financing discipline.

The model breaks when hashprice falls below fleet-and-power cost, collateralized BTC declines, curtailment or interconnection delays reduce utilization, or debt-funded expansion fails to produce per-share cash flow. Capital claims matter: the June offering sold 3.5 million 9.5% preferred shares at $80 for $280 million gross; their $100 liquidation value creates a $350 million senior claim and $33.25 million annual dividends. business.overview:
BitMine's economic engine is now an Ethereum treasury: capital is raised, ETH is acquired and most holdings are staked for protocol yield. The August update reported 5.85M ETH and 5.07M staked; legacy mining and other operating revenue are no longer the useful valuation anchor. The 2.67% seven-day annualized staking yield must also clear $33.25M of annual preferred dividends at full issuance.

The AI transmission channel is indirect and network-based. If AI agents use Ethereum for payments, identity, tokenized assets or coordination, higher settlement demand could support ETH value and staking fees. BitMine itself does not report AI software or data-center revenue, so the channel remains an ETH adoption thesis.

The model breaks if ETH declines, staking yield falls, validators are slashed, custody or smart contracts fail, or issuance grows faster than ETH per diluted common share. Preferred dividends and opaque values for strategic investments also reduce residual NAV available to common holders.
business.moat: BitMine's advantage is capital access and treasury scale: holding 4.8% of ETH supply can support institutional staking operations and market visibility. ETH is fungible, however, and scale is not a moat if financing terms transfer value from common holders or staking execution underperforms.

Q2 gold production was 163,490 ounces, silver production 4.4M ounces and copper production 11.4M pounds; realized prices, grades, recoveries and unit costs set mine margins. The quarter generated $387.5M of free cash flow and left the company with $347M net cash.

The AI transmission channel is through metals and infrastructure, not software. Data-center construction and electrification can support copper and silver demand, but gold still supplied roughly two-thirds of Q2 metal revenue and monetary demand remains the dominant valuation driver.

The model breaks if grades, recoveries or ramp-ups miss plan, if Rainy River or New Afton costs remain elevated, or if gold and silver prices normalize before acquisition synergies arrive. Large purchase-accounting charges and the enlarged share count can also obscure whether growth is accretive per share.
business.moat: Coeur's moat is a diversified, long-life operating portfolio in established North American jurisdictions plus the technical teams and processing infrastructure required to improve acquired mines. Ore bodies are finite, however, and the moat only converts to value through reserve replacement, cost control and disciplined integration.

The AI transmission channel is remote: gold benefits mainly from monetary demand, real rates and risk hedging rather than data-center construction. AI can support broader power and capital spending, but it is not a measurable revenue driver for Equinox and should not inflate mine valuation.

The model breaks if Greenstone or Valentine ramps miss plan, integration fails, gold prices fall toward $1,900-$2,000 guidance AISC, or simultaneous Valentine and South Railroad spending consumes liquidity. Musselwhite, Camino Rojo, Greenstone and Valentine create scale; South Railroad and expansions add duration, but execution and capital discipline determine whether scarce ore bodies translate into per-share value.
